name: Congregational Church / Memorial Hall / Afton Historical Museum
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built in 1868 by the Congregational Church Society, the building was moved to its present location in 1926 after a mudslide. It later became a community meeting hall and the home of the Afton Historical Museum.

name: Cushing Hotel / Afton House Inn
description: Built in 1867, the Cushing Hotel is one of Minnesota's oldest operating hotels and continues as the Afton House Inn.

name: Citizens State Bank / Old Berry Shed
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built in 1913, the bank was robbed in 1921. The former bank and nearby berry shed recall Afton's banking and berry-growing history.

name: Selma's Ice Cream Parlor
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built around 1880, the Holberg home became Selma's ice cream and confectionery parlor and an enduring Afton landmark.

name: Asa and Flora Tracy House
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: The locally designated house is associated with Asa and Flora Tracy, who came to Afton in the nineteenth century.

name: Emil Asp Blacksmith Shop
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built around 1910, Emil Asp's blacksmith shop served local farms and remained in operation until 1922.

name: Afton Town Square Park
address: St Croix Trl S and 34th St
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Included in the original 1855 village map, the park has long been a center for community events and celebrations.

name: Afton Village School
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built in 1876, the village school served local students until teaching ended there in 1903.

name: Carnithan-Squires House
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built in 1876 by carpenter Samuel Carnithan, the house later belonged to Afton merchant Benjamin Squires and his family.

name: Putnam House / Congregational Parsonage
designation: City of Afton designated historic site
description: Built in 1859 by Reverend Simon Putnam, the house also served as the Congregational Church parsonage and a place for village meetings.
